title: 24-Week Recovery Plan
subtitle: Cervical Spondylosis (C5-6) + Lateral Epicondylitis + Weight Loss + Couch to 5K

the_c6_connection.title: The C6 Connection — Why Your Neck and Elbow Are Linked
the_c6_connection.content: Your cervical spondylosis at C5-6 compresses the C6 nerve root, which controls the wrist extensors — the same muscles affected in lateral epicondylitis (tennis elbow). This means your elbow pain isn't isolated; it's part of a kinetic chain that starts at your neck. That's why this plan treats both simultaneously: decompress the nerve root through cervical exercises, while directly rehabilitating the elbow tendon. As cervical symptoms improve, you'll likely see elbow pain reduce too.

phases.name: Foundation
principles: Never push through sharp or radiating pain
Consistency over intensity — daily gentle work beats occasional hard sessions
Build the habit of daily exercise, pain logging, and nutrition tracking
Walking is the only cardio — no running until Phase 2
phases.nutrition: Moderate deficit: ~1,850 kcal/day, 140g protein. Focus on whole foods, SG hawker-friendly options.
avoid: Gripping heavy objects with left hand
Sitting >45 min without a posture break

phases.name: Build
principles: Run-walk intervals start small — respect the 10% weekly increase rule
Monitor pain after every run session
Weight loss should continue at 0.5–1 kg/week
phases.nutrition: Continue deficit. Slightly higher carbs on run days for energy.

phases.name: Advance
phases.focus: Longer runs, maintenance rehab, strength building
principles: Running becomes the primary physical activity
Focus on running form and enjoyment
phases.nutrition: Approaching target weight. May slightly increase calories if energy is low on heavy run days.

phases.name: 5K Ready
phases.nutrition: At or near target weight (77 kg). Transition to maintenance calories if goal reached.

warning_signs.sign: Sharp shooting pain down the arm
warning_signs.action: STOP immediately. This suggests nerve compression. Contact physio.
Stop the current exercise. If it persists >30 min, contact doctor.

warning_signs.sign: Pain that worsens after exercise (not just during)
warning_signs.action: Reduce intensity next session. If it continues 3+ days, see physio.

warning_signs.sign: Neck pain >7/10 that doesn't ease with rest
warning_signs.action: Skip exercises for that day. If it persists 48 hours, see doctor.

warning_signs.sign: Knee pain during or after running
warning_signs.action: Stop running. Return to walking. May need gait re-assessment.

warning_signs.sign: Any new symptoms (dizziness, headaches, balance issues)
warning_signs.action: Stop all exercises. See doctor before continuing.

ergonomic_checklist: Monitor at eye level (use laptop stand + external keyboard)
Feet flat on floor or footrest
Take posture break every 30 minutes (5 chin tucks + 5 shoulder rolls)
Use vertical mouse to reduce wrist extension
Keep frequently used items within easy reach (no overhead reaching)
